utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To begin with, could the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-A, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could we now have the appearances, please. We shall begin with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour. I'm Upawansa Yapa, appearing for the Prosecution with Mr. Norman Farrell. Ms. Adele Erasmus is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ranko Radovic for Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac for Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: John Livingston for Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Luka Susak for Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Petar Pavkovic, appearing here for Vladimir Santic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I should like to remind you briefly of the context within which this Status Conference was convened. It was convened on the basis of Article 65 bis of the Statute -- excuse me -- of the Rules. And Rule 65 bis speaks about the appeals -- speaks about the Status Conference, and this text reads:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: "The Appeals Chamber or an Appeals Chamber Judge shall convene the Status Conference, within 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal, to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person." Therefore, in pursuance of this Rule 65 bis and as of the Status Conference matter of the 13th of September, 2000, it was decided to convene this Status Conference within 120 days, indicated above. There are two aspects of this Status Conference. The first one is to hear the representatives of the parties about the procedure which is underway. You will also have the opportunity to raise any matter which you deem of importance at this stage of the proceedings. And second, it is also -- we turn to the detained, that is, the accused who are present here, and they, as the text of the Rule says, can speak about -- they tell us about the mental and physical condition. This question will be asked later on. However, first I should like to remind you that as regards the decision on the admission by the Appeals Chamber of additional evidence, that decision will be taken as soon as the Appeals Chamber receives all the pieces, that is, all the arguments of the parties. And in line with this, a decision - you have perhaps already received it, or will receive it today - however, a decision was taken at the request of the -- at the request of four appellants - Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, and Drago Josipovic - which allows them additional time to answer. And this supplementary time to reply to the Prosecutor has to do with this question regarding the presentation of evidence. This time has been extended, at the request of the Defence, until the 18th of December, 2000. And when we receive the reply of the Defence within the time limit that has been now extended, then the Chamber will consider all the questions and will make its ruling. I believe that for the time being, these last procedural points which I have just mentioned, if you now have -- if the OTP or parties, if they have any questions to raise or draw attention to of the Appeals Chamber, I believe now is the time to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Livingston.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: I have one matter which I would like to raise about the timetable and it's this: The Appeals Chamber has very kindly given us until the 18th of this month to file a reply to the Prosecution's response to the Rule 115 motions. We have made, both in our original Rule 115 motion and in the draft of the reply which has been prepared, we have asked the Appeals Chamber to allow us an oral hearing on the Rule 115 motion in this case. There are really two reasons for that. Firstly, we would hope that any court would feel that it was assisted in terms of focussing on the issues and being able to pose to the respective advocates any difficulties that they may have with any of the points that they make. We would hope that any Court would be assisted by an oral hearing in doing that and the whole point, in our submission, of a system such as this is to put in written briefs which will cut the amount of time spent on oral arguments down, but not to do away with the oral process all together. The second point is, and this is really the most important point, but if one reads the appellant's brief which has been filed with the Rule 115 motion in Vlatko Kupreskic's case, it is apparent that the additional evidence motion is central to the appellant's brief, and because it is so important to his appeal as a whole -- and if it is just swept aside, for example, on paper without an oral hearing, a very large part of his appeal will be swept aside without any oral hearing at all. In our submission, that is unfair to Vlatko Kupreskic. Even if the Court doesn't think that it is substantially unfair, substantively, I'm sorry, unfair, we would say that it seems to him to be unfair and, in our submission, an appellant is entitled to feel that not only is justice being done but justice is being seen to be done to him in the case of his appeal which he takes very seriously. So I reiterate now that we are asking for an oral hearing. I don't think that would necessarily take that long to deal with, bearing in mind the written briefs that have been put in, but we would not be happy about being shut out of arguing our case before the full Appeals Chamber; in other words, with it just being dealt with on the papers. So that is plainly something that will affect the time schedule and will affect when a decision is made on the Rule 115 motions if the Appeals Chamber agrees to hear the oral argument. That's all I wish to say about that particular matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Livingston. Do other counsel wish to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Ranko Radovic, Defence counsel for Zoran Kupreskic. Mr. President, I think that in this current stage of the proceedings, it would be premature to pass a definite decision with regard to our presentation of additional evidence. Why is this so? We have requested and you have granted to us that the Prosecutor should submit transcripts to us concerning the testimony of one of the protected witnesses. May I finish, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Yapa, do you have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: I have an objection in this way: My learned friend is making reference to a matter which is subject to protective measures and it is a confidential matter. I don't think it could be taken up in this way by my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please wait, Mr. Radovic. Are we in a private session? I think we can go into closed session

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavkovic, as has just been explained, I believe that the Prosecutor has already given his opinion, given his view. Mr. Radovic was speaking about matters which are ex parte and about elements which are -- about pieces of evidence which are covered by confidentiality and protection and cannot be revealed. Now, during the exchange which took place here, do you submit -- if you wish, with regard to what has just been said, to make a motion to the Chamber, you are fully entitled to do that. But matters which were raised by Mr. Radovic cannot be discussed and we shall not go beyond that during this Status Conference. However, if you have a request to make in this regard, you need to send it to the Chamber and it will rule upon it. I hope I have answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Radovic, do you -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to state my views in relation to the proposal made by our calling Mr. Livingston. He suggested that we have an oral discussion on these new submissions and motions. I'm speaking about Mr. Radovic, or rather Mr. Mirjan and Zoran Kupreskic. We agree with this proposal that there be an oral discussion of these additional pieces of evidence, and after all the arguments are presented by both parties, the Chamber can rule. I think that indeed that would be the most efficient way of proceeding and ultimately reaching a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Slokovic-Glumac. Does the Prosecutor wish to tell us what he thinks about the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On this question of an oral hearing, my learned friend Mr. Livingston referred to this matter in his submissions when he filed the motion for additional evidence, and comprehensive and copious submissions were made in moving for the receipt of additional evidence. We have responded adequately and comprehensively to the motion filed by my learned friend. And for the present, I should say that there does not appear to be any reason for an oral hearing. On the material presented before Your Honours, it is open and it is possible for Your Honours to make a ruling without an oral hearing, so I do not see the necessity for an oral hearing. And if it is Your Honours' view that -- if the Chamber views that an oral hearing be heard on this - the matter is not resolved, it is not complete yet, because in respect of additional evidence - we would move that we be permitted to file submissions on the question of the oral hearing on a later date. I thank Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't quite understand. You want us to put something in writing about the oral hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I stated was if the other Defence counsel are joining Mr. Livingston in moving for an oral hearing -- they have not done so up to now. If that is the case, in respect of the additional evidence that they are moving for, we would urge Your Honour to permit us to file written submissions on that question

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you well, what is being asked is that the additional evidence -- the admission of this additional evidence has been requested by -- in writing and by the 18th of December the documents have to be filed. What Mr. Livingston is asking is to hold an oral hearing in order to round off the argument. But they will not be presenting additional evidence at this oral hearing; they are simply asking for an oral hearing, for an oral argument, not to introduce additional evidence, just to have an oral argument. So if you wish, this matter has nothing to do -- there is nothing out of the ordinary that there be an oral hearing. But after we examine the submission in writing and the written argument - and we shall address that on the 18th of December, as I have told you - the Chamber will examine this submission of Mr. Livingston, understanding that Ms. Slokovic-Glumac and Mr. Radovic are endorsing for the two accused, for Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic, that they join this request. We shall examine the submission and we shall keep you informed about -- if the Chamber so decides, we shall let you know about the possible date of an oral hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to join my learned colleagues in proposing an oral hearing so that we would indeed have all the documents put together as well as all our requests related to new evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Susak. The Chamber will take note of this. Yes, Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I also support what Mr. Livingston moved for. Although I don't know what he will be saying exactly, but on the basis of what he has submitted so far in his Defence, it seems to me that it would be acceptable to have it elaborated orally here as well. My client and I both feel that this could be useful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the Appeals Chamber takes note of the fact that the counsel for all the accused have asked, at least at this conference, to hold an oral hearing, pursuant to Article 115, before the Chamber takes the ruling. We shall, of course, keep you informed about the position of the Appeals Chamber and the date of an oral hearing, if it is to take place. Naturally, the oral hearing will take place in order to round off -- if it does take place, it will be held in order to round off the argument which was filed in writing. Are there any other matters to raise at this Status Conference in this particular case? I do not see any. Yes, Mr. Livingston.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am specifically asked to raise one other matter by Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic, which is to reiterate to Your Honour one point which I made back on September 13th, which is that he is particularly anxious that this appeal be dealt with as speedily as it can be. And what we are anxious to avoid is his appeal being held up by quite legitimate applications - I'm not suggesting they wouldn't be - made by other appellants. He's very anxious to know his fate one way or the other, and I would ask you specifically, at his request, to bear that in mind during all your deliberations. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Livingston. I think I said so last time, so I do not think really it is necessary to repeat it, but -- and the Appeals Chamber heard you, and we are speaking only about the application of the Statute of this Tribunal; that is, we are here to dispense justice as fairly as possible and as expeditiously as possible. It must be -- the Court -- the Tribunal must be fair, must take note of the interests of the Defence, but at the same time there is absolutely no reason which could justify the prolongation of anyone's detention pending the judgement. So we -- the Chamber is fully aware of that. However, for the time being it is the Defence which has asked for an extension, for an extension, which has been granted, in order to take note perhaps of the time necessary to prepare the Defence under the best possible conditions. But I wish to rest -- rest assured that all the members of the Appeals Chamber are very aware of this and the decision will be taken with the least possible delay, and we're also there to see that the proceedings take place under the best possible conditions. Beyond that, are there any other questions? No, I do not see any. Now it remains to turn to the accused, the appellants present here, and ask them if they have any questions to raise regarding the conditions of their detention, as is envisaged by the Rules, and to inquire about the state of their mental and physical health. So I'm turning to the accused and also, of course, to their counsel. You may now raise with the Chamber any matters that you wish to inform us. You may speak for yourselves or you can speak through your attorneys. So you do not have any questions, I see for the time being. Before I adjourn this hearing, this Status Conference, we shall keep you abreast of any further developments in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
